scope: dogfood wave 3 — pr-description-check against 19 merged catalog PRs

before.why: rules matched section headings and Chinese phrases only; every body answered all three in English prose

breakingWithoutMigration.mechanism: BREAKING matched any mention, including a body describing the package (breaking changes announced in a BREAKING CHANGE: trailer)
breakingWithoutMigration.fix: anchor the declaration to line start; real trailers still match

whyPassedOnIrrelevantWord.mechanism: a body passed why-missing because it contained 'because `#` is a non-word character' — a regex note, not a motive
whyPassedOnIrrelevantWord.conclusion: keyword matching for motive fails in both directions; narrowed the phrase list AND made the rule a warning

after.remaining: a genuinely thin old body naming no verification

changes.what: a bullet list, or the phrase 'This PR changes', counts as evidence — not only a 概述 heading
changes.test: naming a test count, an audit or a CI result counts
changes.evidence: fenced blocks masked before evidence is read; a pasted stack trace cannot satisfy the check
changes.breaking: only a line-start declaration counts, judged on prose

npxVerified: a real merged PR body -> 0 errors, 2 warns
a body whose only 'because' is a regex note -> 0 errors, 1 warn

pattern: four of four checks dogfooded against their author were enforcing a spelling instead of the property: commit type, heading wording, changelog bracket format, section headings. The property survived every time; the spelling did not. The one rule that is genuinely not decidable from text — motive — is now the only one that warns.
